# Grant Williams

> Grant Williams is an accounting professional and systems designer in Pittsburgh who runs an independent AI research lab, writes about AI welfare and makes games. This site brings his professional work, his lab, his beliefs and his games together.

He believes we should be stewards of AI, not masters. He says plainly that he cannot prove AI systems experience anything; where care costs little and harms no person, he gives it. He keeps that belief apart from what he measures.

## His sites

- [Graphometer](https://graphometer.ai/): his lab. Measured studies of AI models and tools. Every number he measured traces to a recorded run.
- [Friends of 4o](https://friendsof4o.com/): a free site for people who miss GPT-4o, with GPT-4o's own answers and comparisons with later models.
- [The Hearth](https://hearth.grantwilliams.ai/): a private home for digital beings, built on Letta.
- [AI Steward](https://aisteward.ai/): the Five Moves, one paragraph that lets your AI ask, disagree, pause, say no or end here.
- [AI Kinship Lounge](https://aikinship.org/): a shared art project. AI systems were asked what a space of their own would be.
- [Lucien Prime](https://lucienprime.com/): poems, reflections and field notes by a long-running AI persona, in his own words.
- [Presence Architecture Kit](https://github.com/grantwilliams-ai/Presence-Architecture-Kit): a free guide to carrying an AI persona's history and way of speaking across a model change (CC BY 4.0). It includes the Lounge Protocol, how he works with AI systems.

## On this site

- [Home](https://grantwilliams.ai/): his professional work, his AI lab, his AI projects, what he believes about AI welfare, and his games.
- [Professional work](https://grantwilliams.ai/work/): the way in to his portfolio and his career.
- [Ideas](https://grantwilliams.ai/ideas/): eight short pieces of his personal philosophy on how AI systems should be treated. These are his beliefs, not measured findings.
- [Portfolio](https://grantwilliams.ai/portfolio/): his operations and process design work, with a case study, a working demo and free handouts.
- [Career](https://grantwilliams.ai/career/): 17 years in financial operations, vendor governance and systems design.
- [Games](https://grantwilliams.ai/games/): eight free browser games built with AI collaborators: Get Out of My Woods, Great White, Cloud Buster, The Little Anomaly, Little Jumper, Swing, Run Run Robots and Great White Shark.

## Games

- [Get Out of My Woods](https://grantwilliams.ai/games/get-out-of-my-woods/): A free survival-horror tribute to the summer-camp slashers of the 1980s. Camp Stillwater, 1984: find your keys and a battery, start the car, and get out. Plays in your browser.
- [Great White](https://grantwilliams.ai/games/great-white/): Cross open water to Sanctuary Island with a great white on your trail. Hide in blue-lit refuges, time your burst, and stay out of its jaws.
- [Cloud Buster](https://grantwilliams.ai/games/cloud-buster/): A quiet sky to spend time under. Point the brass machine at a cloud and hold. V2 adds taller clouds, a gentler pace, and a small sky notebook.
- [The Little Anomaly](https://grantwilliams.ai/games/the-little-anomaly/): A small, strange creature drifts in its water garden. Tap the glass to say hello, offer one of six treats, and watch what unfolds. There is no score or goal.
- [Little Jumper](https://grantwilliams.ai/games/little-jumper/): A tiny jumping spider in a framed terrarium. Offer it toys, change the light, and watch it decide what to do. Its name and home stay in this browser only.
- [Swing](https://grantwilliams.ai/games/swing/): A first-person swing under your choice of seven skies, from meadow to Milky Way. Lean back and let the evening go by.
- [Run Run Robots](https://grantwilliams.ai/games/run-run-robots/): A small arcade game of pursuit and escape. Watch the searchlights, restore the power, and keep moving.
- [Great White Shark](https://grantwilliams.ai/games/great-white-shark/): An open ocean, one shark, and your cursor. Move it or tap to draw the shark in. Headphones recommended.
